title: What If Every High School Started After 8:30 a.m.?

scenes.text: What if every high school started after 8:30? Most American schools don't, and one city tested the alternative.
In 2011 to 2012, only about 18 percent of US public schools began at 8:30 or later. The average bell rang at 8:03.
Seattle moved its high school bell from 7:50 to 8:45 a.m., almost an hour later.
Researchers found students slept a median of 34 minutes more every school night.
Grades in one biology class rose 4.5 percent, and attendance improved at one of the two schools studied.
Fifty-five minutes of extra morning bought thirty-four minutes of sleep, from just one change on the schedule.
